subject: NordicBank: VPC maintenance choreography — network quiesce, BGP failover & pinning policy
messages:
From: Sven Larsson <sven.larsson@nordicbank.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: Amelie Berg <amelie.berg@nordicbank.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Jun 2025 08:12:00 +0200
Subject: Request: maintenance plan and fallback for VPC patching

Hi Karthik,

We need a detailed maintenance plan for the on-prem/private VPC upgrade next month. Key asks from our side:
- Minimal service interruption for production inference routes (customer-facing endpoints).
- Clear network quiesce steps (what happens to BGP, ARP, and internal route preference).
- Concrete rollback triggers and an evacuation ladder (who performs what and when).
- Confirmation on version pinning policy (when you allow minor vs major bumps).

Can you share a proposed window and the failover choreography? We have NetOps and Security on standby.

Thanks,
Sven
Sven Larsson
Head of Platform Ops — NordicBank

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: Sven Larsson <sven.larsson@nordicbank.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 10 Jun 2025 10:05:00 +0200
Subject: Re: Request: maintenance plan and fallback for VPC patching

Hi Sven / Amelie,

Thanks — outlined initial proposal below. Attaching a short rollback checklist and a network diagram for reference. High-level summary first:

Planned maintenance window
- Target: 2025-07-07 02:00–06:00 CET (low traffic)
- Preflight dry-run: 2025-06-30 02:00–04:00 CET (no tenant traffic, staged VLAN)

Version pinning policy (suggested)
- Default: pin to major.minor (e.g., 1.12.x) for production fleets for 72 hours after upgrade.
- Allow automated micropatch roll-forward for patches tagged "safe" (security-only) after a 24h soak in staging and sign-off by Ops.
- Major versions require explicit approval from customer PC and a canary with 5% traffic for 48h.

Network quiesce choreography
1) Pre-quiesce checks: CV health, KV cache snapshot, in-flight request drain metrics below 1% of baseline.
2) Announce local BGP route-preference flip to secondary fabric (pre-configured preference), do NOT withdraw routes immediately.
3) Initiate application-level conn drain: stop accepting new long-lived socket leases; allow existing requests to finish (grace period: 90s).
4) Trigger ARP/neighbor refresh on maintenance VLAN and force short MAC cache TTL (2s) to avoid stale L2 entries during rebind.
5) Commit node-level upgrade (kernel/driver/agent), then reintroduce routes with original preference after health checks pass.

Rollback triggers (automatic & manual)
- Automatic: p50 latency increase >30% OR p95 increase >40% for 5 consecutive minutes; error rate spike >5% above baseline.
- Manual: NetOps sees persistent BGP flap, hardware memory pressure, or failed KMS handshake.

Evacuation ladder (roles)
- NetOps (NordicBank): immediate BGP preference revert and enforcement of static routes if needed.
- Redwood OnPrem Ops (Neha): start node unwind, restore KV cache snapshot, set feature-flag to pin previous version.
- Redwood Control Plane (Laura): initiate traffic-shelve (per-customer route isolation) and coordinate DNS TTL bump if cutover needed.

Fallback timing and SLA impact
- If automatic rollback triggered, we aim to restore previous software version within 12 minutes for stateless components and 35 minutes for stateful nodes (KV+model cache warm).
- We will notify via PagerDuty and update a shared incident doc (link in attachments).

Next steps
- Confirm window and availability of NordicBank NetOps team for the preflight dry-run.
- Laura will lead canary criteria; Neha will own the rollback checklist.

I can hop on a quick call to walk the steps through — propose Fri 2025-06-13 09:00 CET.

Regards,
Karthik Iyer
Principal Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference

From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, Sven Larsson <sven.larsson@nordicbank.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 10 Jun 2025 14:37:00 +0200
Subject: Re: NordicBank: VPC maintenance choreography — network quiesce, BGP failover & pinning policy

Karthik — looks good. A couple of clarifying notes and additions to protect cold start of model-serving caches:

- Canary shards: we'll route a fixed 5% of traffic to canary instances pinned to new version; canary health gates: model inference success rate (LLM score sanity), tokenization mismatch rate, and end-to-end latency.
- KV cache warming: after a successful canary (12h probe), prime model KV caches with synthetic traces (we will run a warmup job that is idempotent). That job must be gated by a feature-flag so we can abort rapidly.
- BGP behavior: prefer flip to secondary fabric using local-preference change; only withdraw primary routes if there is sustained packet loss >2% for 10 minutes.
- DNS/edge note: if NordicBank uses external edge caches, coordinate TTL drop to 30s 24 hours prior to the window.

I will add the canary health indicators into the shared doc and own the sign-off on canary->ramp.

-laura
Laura Bennett
Director, Product Ops — Redwood Inference

From: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, Sven Larsson <sven.larsson@nordicbank.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Jun 2025 09:02:00 +0200
Subject: Re: NordicBank: VPC maintenance choreography — network quiesce, BGP failover & pinning policy

Quick operational checklist (attached full markdown):
- Preflight (48h): run smoke tests, validate KMS access, export KV snapshot, verify sched capacity.
- T-2h: set maintenance flag on control plane, set DNS TTL->30s, notify customers (if required).
- T-30m: set node drain mode = soft, capture outstanding requests, start 90s graceful drain timer.
- During upgrade step: monitor BGP session state, interface errors, and kernel dmesg for NIC driver warnings.
- Post-upgrade 0–15m: verify p50/p95 within 15% of baseline and no >1% increase in 5xx. If gates fail, trigger immediate rollback.
- Post-upgrade 15–120m: if canary passes, trigger staged ramp (25% -> 50% -> 100%) with 30m observation windows.

Attachments included: private-deploy-rollback-checklist.md (contains exact CLI snippets), vpc-quiesce-network-diagram.png, nordicbank_maintenance_matrix.xlsx

I will be on-call for the dry-run and the main window. Paging policy: NetOps pods first, then Redwood OnPrem Ops.

- Neha
Neha Kapoor
Sr. OnPrem Ops — Redwood Inference
